papers.title: Spatial control of mitochondrial ubiquitination by the AMBRA1-RMC1-HUWE1 axis.
papers.summary: Reviews how cells ubiquitinate outer-mitochondrial-membrane proteins when PRKN/parkin is absent: AMBRA1 builds a recruitment platform where RMC1 positions the E3 ligase HUWE1 at mitochondria, driving ubiquitination and turnover of MFN2 and VDAC1/2, raising questions of how alternative mitophagy pathways are selected and coordinated.

papers.title: Marked for destruction? When S-nitrosylation writes protein fate through metabolic rewiring.
papers.summary: Shows loss of the denitrosylase AKR1A1 increases S-nitrosylation, impairing glycolysis and raising methylglyoxal; carbonyl (glycation) modification then marks KEAP1 for selective autophagic degradation. The authors propose glycation as a metabolic tag for autophagy whose removal may support tumor progression and therapy resistance.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal control of Atg9 vesicle fusion in autophagosome formation.
papers.summary: Demonstrates in yeast that ATG23 stays bound to ATG9 vesicles after their Golgi/endosomal formation, shielding them from premature fusion during cytoplasmic transport. On arrival at the phagophore assembly site, ATG1-mediated phosphorylation of ATG9 releases ATG23, enabling ATG2 recruitment and productive autophagosome formation.

papers.title: Microbiota-derived indole limits Campylobacter jejuni colonization by inhibiting respiration and metabolism.
papers.summary: Inducing colitis with DSS in otherwise resistant conventional mice enabled rapid Campylobacter jejuni colon expansion, with loss of indole-producing microbiota and reduced colonic indole. Indole suppressed C. jejuni respiration and energy genes, and indole or E. coli Nissle 1917 administration cut colonization, defining inflammation-driven colonization resistance.

papers.title: A built-in brake for plant immunity: Resistance (R) protein-mediated immunity is fine-tuned by R gene analogs.
papers.summary: Identifies R8 gene analogs in potato that lack resistance function yet dampen R8-mediated immunity against Phytophthora infestans by interfering with AVR8 recognition and NRC2 helper NLR oligomerization/membrane association. Overexpression compromises R8 resistance, supporting a model where endogenous braking prolongs resistance durability in the field.

papers.title: Diversity of electron-bifurcating CO(2)-fixing supercomplexes in methanogens.
papers.summary: Presents the cryo-EM structure of a C2-symmetric MVH-HDR-FMD supercomplex from Methanothermobacter marburgensis that couples electron bifurcation to CO2 fixation. Its architecture, with two polyferredoxin branches, differs from the D3-symmetric form of class II methanogens, implying an ancestral C2 state and later horizontal acquisition aiding growth in substrate-poor niches.

papers.title: PAX3-SIX2 muscle stem cell heterogeneity drives muscle-specific repair dynamics diversification.
papers.summary: Shows PAX3 marks a heterogeneous subset of quiescent muscle stem cells whose proportion varies by muscle; PAX3+ cells express SIX2 and proliferate and differentiate faster after injury, while PAX3 loss halts proliferation. SIX2 suffices to boost cell-cycle entry, making PAX3-SIX2 status a lever for muscle-wasting therapies.

papers.title: A suite of fluorescent timers for visualizing protein spatiotemporal dynamics in plants.
papers.summary: Systematically tests fluorescent-timer configurations in Arabidopsis, identifying tandem FTs whose maturation kinetics suit slow plant cells. Validated in organelles and used to track protein turnover in autoimmunity, transport under stress, and polarized translocation in cell-fate decisions; a bipartite design mitigates size-related mobility artifacts.

papers.title: Endothelial C/EBPβ/AEP pathway drives vascular deterioration and systemic aging.
papers.summary: Identifies endothelial C/EBPbeta-AEP activation in aging vessels; AEP cleaves NAMPT, depleting systemic NAD+ and driving senescence, vascular dysfunction, and shortened mouse lifespan. AEP ablation, NAMPT-N136A, the AEP inhibitor CP#11a, or NMN supplementation ameliorated vascular aging, with CP#11a most effective, positioning C/EBPbeta-AEP as an aging therapeutic target.

papers.title: Serpin-driven green camouflage and NIR fluorescence in frogs.
papers.summary: Characterizes biliverdin-binding serpins from tree frogs that stabilize biliverdin with hormone-receptor-like affinity, yielding leaf-green camouflage; some lineages produce near-infrared fluorescence. A glassfrog BBS retains binding despite natural proteolytic cleavage, and photoacoustic tomography maps body-wide distribution, informing NIR molecular-probe design.

papers.title: IL-15 signaling during a critical NK cell developmental window subverts maturation and KIR acquisition.
papers.summary: In CD34+ progenitor-derived NK cells, early IL-15 exposure drives aberrant mTOR activation with DNA-methylation and transcriptional changes that suppress maturation and KIR acquisition; withholding IL-15 transiently or adding rapamycin yields more mature, functional NK cells. Matching IL-15/mTOR overactivation signatures appear in post-transplant patient NK cells.

papers.title: Fungal lipase LipA disarms macrophages by remodeling their lipidome, enabling full virulence in immunocompetent hosts.
papers.summary: Identifies the Aspergillus fumigatus conidial surface lipase LipA as an effector-like virulence factor that remodels macrophage lipidomes: it depletes ether-linked phospholipids and PUFA stores, starves eicosanoid production, shifts ceramides toward sphingomyelins to promote host cell survival, and reduces phagocytosis, enabling full virulence in immunocompetent hosts.

papers.title: Temporal CRAC channel blockade modulates the MYC-MXD axis to attenuate autoimmune inflammation.
papers.summary: Shows TH17 cells are uniquely vulnerable to temporal CRAC channel blockade, which disrupts effector function and metabolism; MYC rescues this. CRAC activity maintains MYC by repressing MXD genes, and blocking channels elevates MXD to dampen TH17 pathogenicity in autoimmunity models and human TH17 cells.

papers.title: Viral infection activates the IRF1-BAK axis to drive mitochondria-derived inflammation.
papers.summary: Defines a shared route to virus-triggered inflammation: infection activates STAT1-IRF1, which binds the BAK promoter; mitochondrial BAK accumulation permeabilizes the outer membrane and releases inflammatory DAMPs. Bak knockout protects mice from lethal IAV and SFTSV inflammation, nominating the IRF1-BAK axis as an anti-inflammatory drug target.

papers.title: Defensive lipid droplets are PUFA reservoirs and suppliers driving bacterial clearance and inflammation.
papers.summary: Shows infection- and cytokine-programmed lipid droplets in macrophages become PUFA reservoirs and suppliers. Newly formed droplets accumulate defensive proteins and synthesize PUFAs, with arachidonic acid most metabolized; adipose triglyceride lipase releases it for prostaglandin and thromboxane synthesis, phagocytosis, and bacterial clearance during innate immunity.

papers.title: Toward a more precise immunophenotypic and molecular definition of human cMoPs.
papers.summary: Re-evaluates human common monocyte progenitor definitions, showing CD115+CD64hi/int gating captures cMoPs more accurately than CLEC12A+CD64hi. Differentiation assays, scRNA-seq, and ATAC-seq reveal five transcriptional states, maturation and IFN/stress programs, and candidate regulators IRF8, PU.1, and C/EBPdelta in monocyte development.

papers.title: Dormant bacteria eliminate RNA phages through cumulative ROS-mediated RNA damage.
papers.summary: Explains RNA phage scarcity: they infect growing bacteria efficiently but are gradually eliminated inside dormant cells by weak, time-dependent ROS that cumulatively damages RNA. Mannitol or ROS-degrading enzymes rescue phages; copy number allows occasional survival, reconciling ongoing infection with the rarity of RNA phages in nature.

papers.title: Visualizing the Golgi apparatus and Golgiphagy in vivo.
papers.summary: Introduces reporter mouse lines for constitutive or Cre-dependent Golgi visualization and golgiphagy readout, enabling single-cell quantification across tissues. Basal golgiphagy varies by cell type and tissue, is higher in proximal tubules and cerebellar neurons, and is enhanced by starvation and LPS inflammation, especially in liver, spleen, and kidney.

papers.title: Emerging role for R-loops in chromosome segregation.
papers.summary: Reviews R-loops in chromosome segregation: these RNA-DNA hybrids help ensure faithful mitosis yet, unresolved, destabilize kinetochores and promote chromosomal instability. The authors survey how R-loop dynamics affect centromere function and argue that therapeutic modulation of R-loop handling may benefit diseases including cancer.

papers.title: Nonlinear viscoelastic effects of fascia: experimental findings and constitutive modelling.
papers.journal: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface
papers.summary: Biomechanically characterizes fascia lata with stress-relaxation and dynamic mechanical analysis across orientations, strains, and frequencies. Transverse tissue relaxes more than longitudinal; a two-branch linear visco-hyperelastic model outperformed a single-branch nonlinear one, indicating spectral refinement matters more than nonlinearity for predicting fascial dissipation.

papers.title: HyLnc: a hybrid deep learning and feature-based approach for long non-coding RNA prediction.
papers.summary: Presents HyLnc, combining a BERT-based RNA language model's contextual embeddings with 348 handcrafted ORF, UTR, composition, and Fickett features; feature selection plus random forest classification achieved 91.30% accuracy, F1 91.23%, MCC 82.60 on independent validation, outperforming existing lncRNA prediction tools for transcriptome annotation.

papers.title: Discovery of a small peptide that increases yeast lifespan by enhancing the function of APCCdh1 in nondividing quiescent cells.
papers.summary: Reports a small peptide, C43-4, found via yeast two-hybrid screening against APC10, that extends chronological lifespan of quiescent yeast by enhancing APCCdh1 activity, keeping CLB1 and MPS1 low. Synthetic C43-4 extends lifespan even when added late, and conserved action extends to C. elegans via DAF-16 and AAK-2.

papers.title: Screening for dual sgRNAs with comparable indel efficiencies enhances CRISPR-mediated large-fragment deletion.
papers.summary: Screens 78 sgRNAs across nine gene clusters and 31 large fragments (5-340 kb) to derive CRISPR deletion rules: choose dual sgRNAs with comparable indel efficiencies and use a single pair rather than multiplexing. Following these rules yielded 95% founder transmission of a 340 kb deletion and ~70% average transmission overall.

papers.title: ALMS1 regulates primary cilia signaling in adipogenesis.
papers.summary: Shows ALMS1 loss in visceral adipocyte progenitors blocks adipogenesis, reduces ciliation and centriole cohesion, and leaves ciliary GPCR localization intact while disrupting downstream ciliary signaling, linking the Alström syndrome ciliopathy gene to primary cilium-dependent adipose expansion and metabolic disease.

papers.title: Regulation of TIPIN and replication fork dynamics by USP37.
papers.summary: Demonstrates the deubiquitinase USP37 resides at replication forks and stabilizes TIPIN's chromatin association. USP37-deficient cells under oncogene-induced stress show slowed forks, impaired restart, and nuclease susceptibility, explaining cancer cells' heightened dependence on USP37 and fork-protein regulation in maintaining replication fork function.

papers.title: The evolutionary origins of the parthenogenetic lizard Aspidoscelis tesselatus.
papers.summary: Uses genome-wide sequences and ecological niche modeling to show the parthenogenetic whiptail lizard Aspidoscelis tesselatus arose from a single hybridization between A. scalaris and A. marmoratus under 500,000 years ago, with ongoing de novo mutation, introgression, and break-associated variation shaping a dynamic asexual genome.

papers.title: Mechanistic inhibition of herpes simplex virus-1 UL21 immune-evasion function by natural-product scaffolds: A multi-tier docking, dynamics, and energetic profiling approach.
papers.summary: Virtual-screens African natural-product libraries against HSV-1 UL21, an immune-evasion tegument protein that suppresses cGAS-STING signaling. Docking, molecular dynamics, and free-energy calculations nominate four scaffolds, with kaempferol 3,7,4'-tri-O-beta-glucoside showing the most favorable predicted binding, as candidate UL21 inhibitors.

papers.title: From in silico prediction to experimental validation: Identification of drugs and novel synergistic combinations that inhibit growth of inflammatory breast cancer cells.
papers.summary: Experimentally validates repurposed-drug predictions for inflammatory breast cancer using literature-wide associations and gene reversal rate. In SUM149 cells, predicted compounds showed 70% and 38% success rates respectively; screening identified synergistic IGF-1R/EGFR/PI3K-AKT-mTOR-targeting combinations that reduced pathway phosphorylation, migration, and reversed the IBC expression signature.

papers.title: Hepatic transcriptomic landscape of chicken reveals host responses to spotty liver disease.
papers.summary: Provides liver transcriptomics for chicken spotty liver disease caused by Campylobacter hepaticus: 9,277 differentially expressed genes with strong IL-22, IL-21, IL-6 immune activation and acute-phase SAA induction, alongside profound downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid, iron, and heme metabolism, clarifying host responses behind egg-production losses.

papers.title: Tceal7 is a BRG1-regulated target of calcineurin signaling that promotes myoblast differentiation.
papers.summary: Identifies Tceal7 as a direct target of BRG1-containing SWI/SNF complexes and calcineurin signaling during myoblast differentiation. BRG1 occupancy at the Tceal7 promoter rises with differentiation; calcineurin knockdown or inhibition suppresses Tceal7, and Tceal7 knockdown impairs myogenin expression and dysregulates myogenic, metabolic, and cell-cycle programs.

papers.title: Effectiveness of cold atmospheric plasma on Staphylococcus Aureus colonies on living animal tissue surface.
papers.summary: Tests cold atmospheric plasma devices (dielectric barrier discharge, helium and argon jets) against Staphylococcus aureus on atopic-dermatitis-like skin lesions in living tissue, showing significant bacterial load reduction versus untreated controls, reduced scratching behavior, and characterized heat, UVC, and ozone operator exposure.

papers.title: Substrate morphology modulates bacteriophage mobility and alters bactericidal potency.
papers.summary: Engineers smooth, rough, and porous substrate morphologies and shows phage K bactericidal potency falls as topographic complexity rises, with histology and COMSOL simulations attributing the effect to tortuosity-limited phage access. Substrate morphology should inform phage dosing and design for wound beds and implant interfaces.

papers.title: Tragopogon coelesyriacus Boiss. attenuates ethanol-induced gastric ulcer in vivo: modulation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis.
papers.summary: In an ethanol-induced rat gastric ulcer model, methanolic Tragopogon coelesyriacus extract at 200 and 400 mg/kg improved mucus and acidity defense, raised lesion protection to 51-66%, restored SOD and catalase, lowered MDA and TNF-alpha/IL-6, raised IL-10 and HSP70, lowered BAX, and showed no toxicity over two weeks.

papers.title: FTO-mediated GPX4 m6A modification in ferroptosis-induced DNA damage and inflammatory response during acute lung injury.
papers.summary: In LPS-driven acute lung injury models, FTO reduces m6A modification of GPX4 mRNA, accelerating GPX4 protein degradation and triggering iron accumulation, ROS, lipid peroxidation, DNA damage, ferroptosis, and inflammation. GPX4 m6A-site mutation or FTO silencing protects lung function, positioning FTO-GPX4 as a therapeutic axis.

papers.title: SIRT3-mediated DRP1 acetylation changes are associated with the restoration of mitochondrial function and alleviation of anterior cruciate ligament injury-induced osteoarthritis.
papers.summary: Shows SIRT3 is downregulated in rat osteoarthritis after ACL transection and in IL-1beta-treated chondrocytes. SIRT3 overexpression relieves cartilage pathology, restores mitochondrial function, and reduces ER stress, with altered DRP1 acetylation and abundance linking mitochondrial dynamics to OA progression and mitochondrial-ER crosstalk.

papers.title: The Expression Pattern of HSF1 and Its Regulating HSP70/TLR2 Expression during MO Infection.
papers.summary: In sheep infected with Mycoplasma ovipneumoniae, lung tissue and alveolar macrophages show reduced HSF1 and HSP70 with elevated TLR2. HSF1 overexpression restores HSP70, curbs TLR2 induction, and improves bacterial clearance, delineating an HSF1-HSP70/TLR2 pathway that could guide control strategies for ovine pneumonia.

papers.title: Dopamine receptor D1 is altered in atrial fibrillation-associated tissues and modulates Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte stress partly through PI3K/Akt signaling.
papers.summary: Finds dopamine receptor D1 downregulated in atrial myocardium and epicardial adipose tissue of atrial fibrillation patients and in angiotensin II-infused mice. DRD1 overexpression in cardiomyocytes activates PI3K/Akt and blunts Ang II-induced hypertrophy, ROS, and NLRP3 signaling, though causality for AF susceptibility in vivo remains untested.

papers.title: Synergistic restoration of NK cell cytotoxicity against solid tumors via sLTA-mediated dual-action modulation.
papers.summary: Shows lipoteichoic acid from Latilactobacillus sakei K101 dual-boosts NK cell-based immunotherapy against solid tumors: it upregulates NKG2D and natural cytotoxicity receptors on NK cells while raising MICB and lowering BCL-2 in resistant HT-29 colon cancer cells, restoring caspase-3-dependent killing and TNF-alpha/IFN-gamma-mediated contact-independent cytotoxicity.

papers.title: Amino acid transporters in hepatocellular carcinoma: Gatekeepers of metabolic reprogramming.
papers.summary: Reviews amino acid transporters (PAT, SNAT, xCT, LAT1, ASCT2) as gatekeepers of hepatocellular carcinoma metabolic reprogramming, covering tumor microenvironment effects, signaling, emerging RNA-based therapeutics, small-molecule inhibitors, and combination strategies, plus barriers from tumor heterogeneity, transporter redundancy, off-target toxicity, and resistance.

papers.title: Interleukin-1β potentiates transforming growth factor-β-induced fibronectin expression, migration, and invasiveness of mesenchymal-like SK-Hep1 cells via p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase-SMAD2/3 crosstalk.
papers.summary: In mesenchymal-like SK-Hep1 hepatocellular carcinoma cells, IL-1beta potentiates TGF-beta1-induced fibronectin and N-cadherin expression, migration, and invasion by increasing p38 MAPK phosphorylation and enhancing SMAD2/3 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation; p38 inhibition with SB202190 reduces these mesenchymal phenotypes.

papers.title: Collateral sensitivity-harnessing microbial vulnerabilities as a solution to antimicrobial resistance.
papers.summary: Reviews collateral sensitivity: resistance to one antibiotic can create vulnerability to another, an evolutionary trade-off exploitable against multidrug-resistant bacteria. Laboratory evolution, genome sequencing, deep mutagenesis, and machine learning can design bespoke therapies; translational barriers and design principles for clinical implementation are discussed.

papers.title: Target-Site Selection by Transcription Factors: Roles of DNA, Chromatin, and Cofactor-Mediated Regulation.
papers.summary: Reviews how transcription factors, which recognize short degenerate motifs, select functional target sites in vivo. Layers including DNA methylation, nucleosome organization, histone marks, chromatin remodeling, TF oligomerization, localization, and especially DNA-binding-domain-directed cofactor regulation shape selective occupancy across mammalian genomes.
